newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE FASTEST BUT STILL HAS DOUBTS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE FASTEST BUT STILL HAS DOUBTS.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve was still far from confident of a second successive British Grand Prix win despite claiming pole with a late attacking drive in qualifying on Saturday.

The Williams driver moved to the head of the time-sheets in the closing minutes of the hour-long session with a time of one minute 21.598 seconds to displace team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany and Finn Mika Hakkinen in a McLaren.

But the competitiveness of his rivals, with less than eight tenths of a second covering the top 11 drivers, left Villeneueve convinced that only a perfect race would be enough for a driver to finish in the points.

"It is possible to have a really quick car and still not finish in the points," said the 26-year-old Canadian. "But I am happy to be on pole position because this is a very difficult track to get the most out of yourself on.
"I was annoyed to see Heinz-Harald on pole near the end of the session because he was quite a bit slower than me in practice and I knew I didn't want him to be ahead of me.
"I saw a cloud come over, which slightly cooled the track and made the car faster, and I just went for it. It was very enjoyable."
Villeneuve is second in the drivers world championship table, 14 points adrift of German Michael Schumacher.
Frentzen had seemed destined to claim the second pole position of his career when he set his best lap of 1:21.732 with just four minutes of the session remaining.
But although it left Frentzen disappointed it left the Williams team occupying the front two positions on the grid for the first time since the Spanish Grand Prix in Barcelona in May.
"I was very annoyed when he got it back at the last moment," said the German. "My main complaint has been traffic today because on all of my runs I came across traffic."
The most disappointed man was Hakkinen, however, who dropped from pole position to third on the grid in the closing four minutes after the Williams cars bettered his time.

"I am not really happy," he said. "I was really confident I could be in pole position, even after the Williams cars went out, but unfortunately there were cars in front of me which meant I could not run at the maximum."
World championship leader Schumacher qualified in fourth in a Ferrari after being unable to match the pace of the Williams or McLaren, while his brother Ralf will start fifth for Jordan.
Reigning world champion Damon Hill enjoyed a much better showing after a weekend so far dominated by off-track talk of team disputes by setting the 12th best time for Arrows.
Briton Eddie Irvine in the other Ferrari was lucky to qualify in seventh after hitting a hare on one of his quick laps.
"I got a big fright. I was forced to pit to have the car checked and tyres changed," he said.
